name: FFGame
rootCause: By deploying the attack contract and using the same algorithm as FFgame to calculate the random number in the contract, the attacker immediately uses the random number attack contract in inline_action after generating the random number, resulting in the winning result being "predicted", thus reaching the super high winning rate.

descriptions.text: By deploying the attack contract and using the same algorithm as FFgame to calculate the random number in the contract, the attacker immediately uses the random number attack contract in inline_action after generating the random number, resulting in the winning result being "predicted", thus reaching the super high winning rate.

FFGame, an EOS-based gaming dApp, was exploited on November 8, 2018, due to its use of predictable random number generation. The attacker repeatedly won by precomputing outcomes, resulting in the loss of approximately 1,331 EOS (roughly $7,200 at the time). Funds were transferred to the Huobi exchange, with no public evidence of recovery or patch from developers. FFGame's smart contract relied on deterministic on-chain data for randomness. This made its random number generation predictable, allowing an attacker to precompute game outcomes and place winning bets with high accuracy.
